newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit slides as dollar rises on Iraq attack.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit slides as dollar rises on Iraq attack.

text.p: The ringgit was shaken from weeks of stupor to end lower as the dollar jumped on news of a U.S. missile attack on Iraq.
Dealers said the afternoon surge of the dollar/majors was quickly reflected in the ringgit.

But they were mixed on the ringgit's immediate direction, as a lot depends on whether temperatures in the Middle East will rise further. "Will there be more attacks? That is the main question for the dollar," said one local bank dealer.
At the 1000 GMT local close, ringgit was at 2.4966/71 per dollar against 2.4933/38 on Monday.
Research house MMS International said in a Tuesday commentary that dollar/ringgit could gain more on dollar bullishness and expectations of higher U.S. interest rates.

The Wall Street Journal reported in its Tuesday edition that U.S. Federal Reserve policy makers are mulling a 50-point hike in interest rates unless clear signs of slower growth emerge in the next three weeks.
In the interbank market, the overnight rate kept to a high level, ending at 8.50/70 percent from 8.70 previously. Activities remain centered on the short-term tenures.
